The best fit is dP/dt ≈ 0.344·t·√P + f(P), where f(P) is a smooth function of P that I could only approximate with a mix of √P, 1/P, P·ln P, P^1.5, exp(−P), and P·exp(−P) terms. The t·√P coefficient was stable across all fits at about 0.344, but f(P) never reduced to a short closed form.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):
    a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,k,m=params[:10]
    s=np.sqrt(P); L=np.log(P)
    return a + b*s + c/P + d*t*s + e*P*L + f*P**1.5 + g*np.exp(-P) + h*P + k*P*np.exp(-P) + m*L/P
